Every prop has one of five jobs

Lesson 1 · Slots and compound components

Let the consumer own the markup

<Select value={jobType} onChange={setJobType}>
  <Select.Trigger placeholder="Job type" />
  <Select.List>
    <Select.Option value="full-time">Full-time</Select.Option>
    <Select.Option value="contract">Contract</Select.Option>
    <Select.Option value="internship">Internship</Select.Option>
  </Select.List>
</Select>

Share state through context

The root owns the state and provides it; each Select.Option reads it with useContext — at any depth, through any wrapper the consumer adds.

Not cloneElement

Children.map plus cloneElement only reaches direct children. Wrap one option in a layout div and it silently stops working.

Lesson 1 · Controlled vs uncontrolled

Who owns the value? Support both.

Controlled · the parent owns it

Validate, format or sync it on every keystroke.

<SearchBox value={q} onChange={setQ} />

Uncontrolled · the component owns it

Seed it once, read it on submit. No parent re-render per key.

<SearchBox defaultValue="react" />
function useControllableState<T>(value: T | undefined, defaultValue: T, onChange?: (v: T) => void) {
  const [inner, setInner] = useState(defaultValue);
  const isControlled = value !== undefined;
  const current = isControlled ? value : inner;
  function set(next: T) {
    if (!isControlled) setInner(next);   // uncontrolled: keep it ourselves
    onChange?.(next);                     // either way: tell the parent
  }
  return [current, set] as const;
}

Lesson 1 · Design tokens

A token is a decision with a name

:root {
  --blue-500: #2196F3;  --red-500: #E5484D;  --space-2: 8px;   /* primitives: raw values */
  --color-accent: var(--blue-500);                               /* semantic: what it means */
  --color-danger: var(--red-500);
  --color-surface: #FFFFFF;
}
[data-theme="dark"] { --color-surface: #0E1525; }                /* a theme swaps the semantic layer */
.button { background: var(--color-accent); padding: var(--space-2); }
Components read semantic tokens only. Dark mode is a second set of semantic values — not a second stylesheet.

Lesson 1 · Container queries and fluid type

Ask the container, not the window

.job-list { container-type: inline-size; }

.job-card { display: grid; gap: var(--space-2); }                   /* narrow: stacked */
@container (min-width: 36rem) {
  .job-card { grid-template-columns: 4rem 1fr auto; }               /* wide: logo · details · save */
}

h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1.25rem + 2vw, 3rem); }               /* fluid, with a floor and a ceiling */
The same JobCard sits in a narrow sidebar and a wide feed on one screen. A media query sees one window; a container query sees the space each card was actually given.

Lesson 2 · The accessibility tree

Role, name, state — or it isn't there

What you wrote

<div className="save" onClick={save}>
  <StarIcon />
</div>

Tree: generic · no name · not focusable. Tab skips it, Enter does nothing.

What the tree needs

<button type="button" onClick={save}
  aria-label="Save job" aria-pressed={saved}>
  <StarIcon aria-hidden="true" />
</button>

Tree: button · “Save job” · pressed. Spoken roughly as “Save job, toggle button, pressed”.

ARIA only edits the tree — it adds no behaviour. A div with role="button" still needs tabindex, Enter and Space. The native element brings all three, so it comes first.

The roles lessons 3 and 4 build to

RoleOnMust carry

listbox · optionThe suggestions popup, each rowA name on the listbox; a unique id and aria-selected on every option
dialogThe modal panelaria-modal="true", aria-labelledby → its heading
tablist · tab · tabpanelThe tabsaria-selected on each tab, aria-controls → its panel
statusThe toast regionImplicitly aria-live="polite"; mounted empty, before the first message
A component isn't finished when it looks right. It's finished when the tree says what the screen shows.

Lesson 2 · Focus and the keyboard path

Tab between widgets, arrows within

Roving tabindex · focus moves

One item has tabIndex 0, the rest -1. Arrows move the zero and call .focus(). Tabs, toolbars, menus.

tabIndex={i === active ? 0 : -1}
// on ArrowRight:
setActive(next); refs[next].focus();

aria-activedescendant · focus stays

DOM focus never leaves the input; it points at the highlighted option's id. Comboboxes — the user keeps typing.

<input role="combobox"
  aria-activedescendant="q-opt-3" />
// focus stays here; the tree reads option 3
Fifty jobs in a list are one Tab stop, not fifty. tabindex="0" joins the order, "-1" is focusable by script only, and a positive tabindex is always a bug.

Lesson 3 · Build · The ARIA combobox

The autocomplete, as the tree sees it

<label htmlFor="q">Search jobs</label>
<input id="q" role="combobox" value={query} onChange={onType} onKeyDown={onKey}
  aria-autocomplete="list"
  aria-expanded={open}
  aria-controls="q-list"
  aria-activedescendant={open && active >= 0 ? 'q-opt-' + active : undefined} />
<ul id="q-list" role="listbox" aria-label="Job suggestions" hidden={!open}>
  {jobs.map((job, i) => (
    <li key={job.id} id={'q-opt-' + i} role="option" aria-selected={i === active}
        onMouseDown={e => e.preventDefault()} onClick={() => choose(job)}>{job.title}</li>
  ))}
</ul>
↓ ↑ move the active option (↓ opens the list) · Enter chooses · Escape closes, a second one clears · typing keeps editing. DOM focus never leaves the input.

Lesson 3 · Build · Race conditions

Whichever response lands last wins

Debounce waits for typing to pause, so fewer requests start. It does nothing about the order they come back in.

Debounce decides how many requests run. Only cancelling — or ignoring — the stale one decides which result renders. You need both.
MODULE 07 · VIDEO 3
14 / 27
Lesson 3 · Build · Debounce and abort

One effect: wait, fetch, cancel

useEffect(() => {
  if (query.trim().length < 2) { setJobs([]); return; }
  const ctrl = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => {                          // debounce: wait for a pause
    fetch('/api/jobs?q=' + encodeURIComponent(query), { signal: ctrl.signal })
      .then(res => res.json())
      .then(setJobs)
      .catch(err => { if (!ctrl.signal.aborted) setError(err); });
  }, 250);
  return () => { clearTimeout(timer); ctrl.abort(); };   // the next keystroke cancels both
}, [query]);
The cleanup is the fix: a new keystroke clears the timer that hasn't fired and aborts the request already in flight, so a stale response can never reach setJobs.

Lesson 4 · Build · The modal

Trap focus, then give it back

function openModal() {
  returnTo.current = document.activeElement as HTMLElement;   // remember the trigger
  setOpen(true);                                               // an effect focuses the first field
}
function onKeyDown(e: React.KeyboardEvent) {
  if (e.key === 'Escape') return closeModal();
  if (e.key !== 'Tab') return;
  const items = Array.from(panel.current!.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(FOCUSABLE));
  const first = items[0], last = items[items.length - 1];
  if (e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === first) { e.preventDefault(); last.focus(); }
  if (!e.shiftKey && document.activeElement === last) { e.preventDefault(); first.focus(); }
}
function closeModal() { setOpen(false); returnTo.current?.focus(); }
Native <dialog> with showModal() makes the page behind inert and closes on Escape for free. Labelling it, and checking focus lands back on the trigger, stay your job.

Every overlay has a keyboard contract

WidgetKeysWhere focus goes
Modal
dialog		Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside · Escape closesInside on open; back to the trigger on close
Dropdown menu
aria-haspopup="menu"		Enter Space ↓ open · ↑ ↓ Home End move · Escape closesInto the menu (roving tabindex); back to the button on close
Tabs
tablist · tab		← → move and activate · Home EndOne Tab stop for the whole tablist; Tab again enters the panel
Toast
role="status"		None of its ownNowhere — a toast never takes focus
A dropdown of navigation links is a disclosure, not a menu: a button with aria-expanded and a plain list of links. role="menu" promises app-style arrow keys — use it only if you build them.

Lesson 4 · Build · Toasts and live regions

Announce it without moving focus

// Mounted once, empty, at the app root: a live region must exist before its text changes
<div role="status" className="sr-only">{announcement}</div>

function toast(message: string) {
  setToasts(list => [...list, { id: crypto.randomUUID(), message }]);   // the visible stack
  setAnnouncement('');                                                   // clear first, so the same
  setTimeout(() => setAnnouncement(message), 50);                        // text twice is still read
}
Polite (role="status") for “Job saved”. Assertive (role="alert") only for what must interrupt, like “Session expired”. A toast that holds a button must not vanish on a timer.

Lesson 5 · Forms without a library

Keep the rules, own the messages

<form noValidate onSubmit={onSubmit}>                  {/* keep the checks, drop the browser bubbles */}
  <label htmlFor="email">Email</label>
  <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required
    aria-invalid={Boolean(errors.email)} aria-describedby="email-error" />
  <p id="email-error">{errors.email}</p>
</form>

function messageFor(input: HTMLInputElement) {
  const v = input.validity;                              // the browser already ran the rules
  if (v.valueMissing) return 'This field is required';
  if (v.typeMismatch) return 'Check the format, like name@company.com';
  if (v.tooShort)     return 'Use at least ' + input.minLength + ' characters';
  return '';
}
noValidate turns off the browser's bubbles, not its checks. validity still works, and your message, linked by aria-describedby, is the one a screen reader reads.

Lesson 5 · Validation timing

Submit checks all; blur checks one

function onSubmit(e: React.SubmitEvent<HTMLFormElement>) {
  e.preventDefault();
  const form = e.currentTarget;
  const next = validate(form);                        // messageFor() on every field → { name: message }
  setErrors(next);
  const first = Object.keys(next)[0];
  if (first) return (form.elements.namedItem(first) as HTMLElement).focus();
  apply(new FormData(form));                           // valid: send it
}
WhenWhat you do
SubmitValidate every field, show every error, move focus to the first invalid one.
BlurValidate the field just left — only if the user changed it.
TypingClear an error the moment it's fixed. Never show a new one mid-word.

Lesson 6 · Build · Windowing

Render only what's on screen

const ROW = 96, OVERSCAN = 4;
const start = Math.max(0, Math.floor(scrollTop / ROW) - OVERSCAN);
const end   = Math.min(jobs.length, Math.ceil((scrollTop + viewportHeight) / ROW) + OVERSCAN);
// outer element: height = jobs.length * ROW, so the scrollbar stays honest
// each row in [start, end): position: absolute; transform: translateY(index * ROW)
Ten thousand jobs in memory, about twenty rows in the DOM — at any scroll position.

Lesson 6 · Build · Pooling and recycling

Recycle the node, change its data

Appending forever

Infinite scroll that keeps appending cards: every node costs memory, style and layout work. Page fifty scrolls worse than page one, and garbage-collection pauses show up as jank.

A fixed pool

Build two pages of nodes once. When the top page scrolls out of view, move those nodes to the bottom and give them new text and a new position. Nothing is created or destroyed.

const recycled = pool.splice(0, PAGE);                        // the page that scrolled out of view
pool.push(...recycled);                                      // …moves to the bottom of the pool
recycled.forEach((el, k) => {
  const index = end + k, job = jobs[index];
  el.querySelector('.title')!.textContent = job.title;       // new text, same node
  el.setAttribute('aria-posinset', String(index + 1));       // the tree knows where it is
  el.style.transform = 'translateY(' + index * ROW + 'px)';   // moved by the compositor, no layout
});

Lesson 6 · Build · The whole machine

Two phases: warm up, then recycle

class VirtualList {
  async onBottomVisible() {                          // an IntersectionObserver on the bottom sentinel
    const page = await this.getPage(this.end);
    if (this.pool.length < this.limit) {             // warm-up: create nodes, once
      const frag = document.createDocumentFragment();
      for (const job of page) { const el = this.render(job); this.pool.push(el); frag.append(el); }
      this.list.append(frag);
    } else {                                         // steady state: recycle the top page
      const recycled = this.pool.splice(0, this.pageSize);
      this.pool.push(...recycled);
      recycled.forEach((el, k) => this.update(el, page[k]));
    }
    this.position();        // translateY for every node in the pool
    this.moveSentinels();   // top sentinel above the first node, bottom one below the last
    this.end++;
  }
}
